paper.title_en: Development and performance of a time projection chamber prototype with UV laser tracks for the future e$^+$e$^-$ collider
paper.abstract_en: In future e$^{+}$e$^{-}$ collider projects such as the International Linear Collider (ILC), the Circular Electron-Positron Collider (CEPC), and the Future Circular Electron Positron Collider (FCC-ee), all detector concepts require main tracking detectors with extremely high performance. Time projection chambers (TPCs) are an essential option for large main-tracker detectors. To meet updated physics requirements for high position resolution and particle identification, a TPC prototype integrated with a UV laser track system has been developed at the Institute of High Energy Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences. This paper describes the detector readout, drift chamber, field cage, 266 nm UV laser track system, fast electronics, and data acquisition. Experimental measurements and analysis results obtained in the laboratory show that the TPC prototype was successfully developed and commissioned. The spatial resolution is better than 100 $\mu $m along the drift length. The specific energy loss (dE/dx) resolution is critical for particle identification and separation in the TPC prototype. The feasibility of this method with UV laser tracks was verified for the baseline detector concept of the CEPC. The estimated dE/dx resolution is better than 4% without a magnetic field. Based on this prototype, the pixelated readout TPC was also considered and simulated in the CEPC community.
